rubric_notes: Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct 2.08 lineage; four curated families with correct SUNIDs; a.22.1.0 'not a true family' and the a.22.1.1 octamer comment are both supported by the bundle. Clearly states superfamily-level probable common ancestry with families kept separate, notes the fold held only one superfamily in the retrieved child list, and explicitly rejects transferring nucleosome assembly, TFIID activity, oligomeric state, ligand state, or templates without domain-specific evidence. Complete on all must_include criteria.

Correct domain and family SUNIDs, superfamily a.204.1 SUNID 101386, boundaries match. States probable common ancestry at superfamily level, not fold-only or same-family. Rejects transfer of reaction, substrate specificity, ligand preference, pathway role, oligomeric state. Annotation claims (structural genomics target, Li/UNL, no warnings) are supported by bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct SCCS and SUNIDs for all three families, superfamily c.55.1/53067, fold c.55, class c, plus the duplication annotation, all confirmed by the bundle. Distinguishes superfamily-level homology from fold-only similarity, infers a shared actin-like ATPase structural/evolutionary core, and explicitly refuses to transfer substrate, cellular role, regulation, oligomeric state, whole-protein function, or template choice, noting the external evidence required. No material issues.

Complete. Correct identifiers for class, fold 47239, superfamily 47240, and all three families; fold core and bimetal-centre comments supported by bundle annotations; fold-level homology-not-implied point supported by the a.25 homology response. States superfamily is the deepest shared level, interprets as probable common ancestry with functional divergence, enumerates each forbidden cross-family transfer, and lists residue-level alignment, ligand-bound structures, phylogenetic and biochemical evidence as needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families and SUNIDs within b.6.1/49503, fold b.6/49502, class b; states probable remote common ancestry because deepest shared level is the superfamily; refuses copper, redox, electron-transfer partner and copper-site template transfer; cites both 'lacking the metal-binding site' annotations; requires residue-level conservation plus ligand-bound structural, biochemical, redox or literature evidence. Fully supported. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

All SCCS and SUNIDs (54237, 54250, 54263, 54236, fold 54235) and Pfam links verified against the bundle. Correctly frames sibling families within a homology-bearing superfamily, infers probable common ancestry and shared beta-grasp core, and rejects cross-family transfer of covalent ubiquitin-like modifier function, Ras-binding annotations, and UBX-specific annotations, naming the external evidence types needed. p97 is not named explicitly but UBX-specific function transfer is rejected, which is scientifically equivalent. The unrelated b.34 domain listing in the bundle is not used in the answer and does not detract. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

All classifications and SUNIDs (families, superfamily 52172, fold 52171, class 51349) correct and supported. Distinguishes superfamily homology from same-fold resemblance and from same-family relationship; rejects transfer of canonical phosphorylatable receiver chemistry and of PLP decarboxylase activity; cites the KaiA annotation; lists needed external evidence. Omits explicit rejection of circadian-regulation transfer. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Correct b.84 > b.84.5 > b.84.5.1 placement, fold comment, sibling superfamilies, PubMed xref, all verified. Identifies superfamily as the homology-bearing level, probable common ancestry within b.84.5/b.84.5.1, fold sharing supports topology only, and explicitly states the split is not independent evidence of convergence or independent origin; notes the API does not expose the curator rationale. No SUNIDs given but all SCCS identifiers correct; family-vs-superfamily handled adequately.

Correctly separates f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3 (SUNIDs 81342/81343/103501) under fold f.21 (81344) in 2.08; example lineages d1bccc3, d1e7pc_, d1q16c_ all match the bundle. States fold node does not imply homology above superfamily (supported by homology endpoint), cites f.21.3 'possible link' and f.21.2 one-vs-two-chain comments (both supported), refuses function/template transfer, and lists required external evidence (sequence correspondence, residue-level structural alignment, conserved heme ligands, complex context, phylogeny/literature). Calibrated; does not assert absolute non-homology. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers for the three families, superfamily c.2.1/51735, fold c.2 and class c/51349. Identifies c.2.1 as the deepest common homology-bearing node, reads the relationship as remote homology plus strong functional divergence, and explicitly forbids transferring CoA binding, channel regulation, NAD vs NADP preference, catalytic chemistry, substrate specificity, oligomeric state or whole-protein function without external evidence. The c.2.1.1 comment and the statement that homology warnings/heterogeneity/repeat records are empty are both consistent with the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Gives the full shared lineage through family k.40.1.1 sunid 100905, cites the 'not a true family' comment, states that the grouping cannot be used as a normal family-homology example, and names the external evidence needed for a stronger claim. No factual errors; identifiers supported by the bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct 1.69 (d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 own fold/superfamily; d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; shared class only) and 2.08 (d1t1ja1 A:1-118, SUNID 106249, c.23.14.2 under c.23.14; d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1). Frames change as same-superfamily/different-family probable common ancestry, rejects family membership and function/substrate/oligomer transfer, cites the bundle-supported superfamily comment on active-site similarity, and states that SCOPe does not expose the alignment or curator rationale. Complete.

Gives full b.1.1.1 lineage for d1a14h1 (H:9-111) and full class l / l.1.1.1 Tags / N-terminal Tags / Synthetic lineage for d1a14h2 (H:1-8). Correctly cites homology_implied_by_level=false and artifact_not_homology_evidence (supported), states a tag match supports only an artifact explanation absent independent evidence, and recommends excluding the tag from representative/template/benchmark use. Complete with stated limits. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers, SUNIDs, boundaries, and both divergent 2.08 lineages, plus an unusually careful point that the C-terminal SCOPe domain still contains the conventional domains II to IV, so this is a curated boundary change rather than one SCOPe domain per conventional domain. Correctly refuses cross-module homology, interchangeable roles, and full-length template claims from placement alone. The 2.04 release of the split is not stated.

Correct SIDs, boundaries, and SCCS; mosaic conclusion; A:47-697 placed in Prp8-specific d.394 rather than an older fold; remote-ancestry inference bounded by superfamily semantics with catalytic/ligand caveats and external evidence requirement. Bundle supports. Evaluator: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy; chain lengths 51/442/794 supported by chain endpoints; whole-chain domains correctly noted; re flag, single-repeat comment, canonical representative repeat; explains family as homologous repeat modules in different copy numbers; explicit unsafe-transfer limits and required evidence.

Correct bundle-supported metadata (2.08, 2.08-stable, dates, 2.08-2026-08-16); recommends pinning 2.08 over an unpinned current lookup and avoids calling the periodic label a stable release. Omits advice to preserve the dated label when using periodic-only entries, and instead of stating the periodic semantics (new PDB entries added without rewriting stable domains) only says the metadata does not prove what changed. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct lineage with SUNIDs for d1br0a_, d1ez3a_, d1dn1b_; ms inconsistency and fragment comment; automated match to d3c98b_. Explicitly runs the interpretation from the complete domain to the fragments: partial cores classified with the full STAT-like syntaxin domain, not representatives of a spectrin-repeat topology; keeps the spectrin note as a fragment annotation; advises using fragments only for the covered region or stratifying them; names the external evidence needed. Minor: names only d1ez3a_ of the three 1ez3 chains (identical copies), not material. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers for c.2/c.2.1 and c.3/c.3.1, correct reading of the homology endpoints (superfamily implies homology; folds carry the above-superfamily warning), and the actual c.2 comment about similar nucleotide-binding modes in the next two folds, all supported by the bundle. Reasoning is explicitly asymmetric: divergence within superfamily, convergence compatible but not proven across folds, and neither homology nor independent origin can be asserted from hierarchy alone. Lists appropriate external evidence and rejects function/template transfer from cofactor or active-site similarity. Only two folds exemplified, but no errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Gives both release states with correct codes, descriptions, and the A:500-644 boundary, notes the deepest 2.04 shared node was class b only, and concludes same superfamily but different families in 2.08 as a probable-remote-homology call. Multiple evidence types: the b.18 9-strand two-sheet jelly-roll annotation and the PubMed 17977833 family comment linking d1nqdb_, d1w99a3, and d2quoa_, with d1w99a3 placed in the same family as the Cry3A domain. Explicitly withholds ligand, receptor, calcium, and whole-protein function transfer and restricts template use to the conserved core. Eval: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct SUNIDs, SCCS, lineage, boundaries, and comments; homology within the family retained and explicitly not erased by the warning; hf correctly described as non-inherited, domain-level, different fold with similar sequence/SSE count, reported via both annotations and homology endpoints; rejects interchangeable template/benchmark-positive use; lists external evidence needed (residue-level alignment, state comparison, biochemical data); recommends excluding, stratifying, or keeping d1ztra1 with the hf label. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct release, SUNID 49266, boundaries, protein nodes, and fr definition, all supported. Preserves family homology; aligns only over covered core, masks/labels missing region, and refuses to score full-domain coverage; excludes or stratifies the fragment in complete-domain representative sets while allowing it as an explicitly marked fragment; correctly notes quality ranking would need ASTRAL records not retrieved; separates two protein nodes from truncation-driven diversity; limits function transfer. Meets all must_include items. Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Recommends new superfamily in the existing fold, identifies family/superfamily as the homology-bearing levels and fold as arrangement/topology only, explains why a new family is too strong and a new fold is unjustified when topology matches, lists non-transferable properties, and enumerates the evidence (global core alignment, sequence/motif correspondence, domain context, phylogeny, biochemistry, literature) needed to move into an existing superfamily or to justify a new fold. No identifiers cited; no factual errors. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family SCCS and names, superfamily d.144.1/56112, fold d.144/56111, class d, and fold annotation, all supported by the bundle. Identifies the superfamily as the deepest shared node and draws the probable-common-ancestry and shared PK-like framework conclusion while noting the groups are distinct families. Rejects transfer of Ser/Thr/Tyr recognition, aminoglycoside specificity/resistance, lipid substrate choice, and PI3K regulatory mechanisms. Requires sequence/structure alignments, equivalent active-site and ligand-bound evidence, biochemical substrate/regulation assays, domain context, and phylogenetic/literature support. Complete.
